review_scope: AI maintainer adjudication for two code_assist commit-level web bundle candidates. This review decides train-support and repo-overlap stress-eval admissibility only, not source-heldout headline admissibility.

bundle_reviews.subject: ui: expose latest verdict endpoint in dashboard
rationale: The diff adds a new backend API route and the dashboard JS/UI reads from it, so the behavior-owning surface is the FastAPI backend even though multiple asset files change.
The selected verifier anchor is relevant: the dashboard API integration tests are maintainer-meaningful and provide a visible verification surface.
The candidate set is competitive enough to avoid trivial one-token routing, but same-repo overlap means this should not be treated as heldout headline evidence.
shortcut_risks: FastAPI route additions may bias the model toward backend ownership without proving it read the verifier/test evidence.
The commit subject names 'endpoint', which correlates with backend ownership and should not be shown verbatim in prompt-visible evidence.
recommended_use: Allow as standalone train-support web bundle after prompt-visible evidence strips commit subject leakage.
Allow as harness or standalone repo-overlap stress-eval bundle.
Do not use for source-heldout headline web claims.

bundle_reviews.subject: updates
rationale: This commit changes JS, HTML, and backend route handling together. The backend remains the most plausible behavior owner when judged against the dashboard API verifier anchor.
The competing frontend surfaces remain plausible enough to make localization nontrivial, which is useful for train-support and stress evaluation.
The lack of a descriptive commit subject reduces one shortcut channel relative to the later verdict commit.
shortcut_risks: Because the verifier anchor is integration-heavy, the model may still learn a backend-prior from test style rather than from the specific changed behavior.
Same-repo overlap remains the main claim boundary; this is not a heldout repo-family win.
recommended_use: Allow as standalone train-support web bundle after commit metadata stays hidden from prompts.
Allow as repo-overlap stress-eval bundle to test whether the 100M still generalizes across distinct UI commit roots in the same repo.
Do not use for source-heldout headline web claims.

next_best_step: Project these two adjudicated code_assist commit-level bundles into compact standalone rows and harness stress-eval rows, while keeping source-heldout headline web claims frozen until a non-overlapping repo family exists.
